SP-9.5.status_claim: implemented on domains-framework/3; framework check (base.check, every configuration) and the gate test queued in a slot job on a snapshot of the branch head (results below when they arrive)
SP-9.5.notes: Migrated to domains-framework/3 in the fourth session (a278fb9, af6a2a9, 0b72492): objective from a goal generator (GoalFamily over a registered evaluator-only metric, parameters drawn from the generator's own stream), Domain.evaluate reads the generated parameters, evidence functions return recorded event sequence numbers, the structure hook reads built state only, the reference reads only the objective text and runs isolated. sci repaired (DEF-I-5): datasheet abs+rel precision, generalised chi-square with propagated calibration covariance, standards-bureau blind challenges at novel conditions; lawlang +5 families (3-variable and held-out). Population researchers scipop (FR-SCIPOP-1). Evaluator: novel-condition nRMSE + co-discovery priority + no copy + independent consistent replications (D-52). Reference (joint fit of law and calibration with certified anchors) succeeded on bench seeds 0, 1, 2 in unofficial runs once the co-discovery rule applied. Fourth session: the standards bureau publishes its challenges as itself (an institution's decision). The structural evaluation configuration (heldout: a law outside the handbook, one standard) was infeasible for the reference (nRMSE 3.2); with five general response shapes beyond the handbook and a nominal-unit-gain prior (the gain is unidentifiable from one standard) the reference succeeds there on seeds 0 and 1 (nRMSE 0.034 / 0.05, local runs) while population researchers still know only the handbook.

limitations: Every coefficient of the three new population modules (scipop, devpop, commlife) is set by hand (plausible, unvalidated; FIDELITY_REGISTER).

The software capabilities are a fixed catalogue of 8 small pure functions; developers' glue code is generated from a package's API by function name, so a package whose function is named differently is not found.
Population researchers know a public handbook of response forms that contains the hidden law families of the training configurations (the structural evaluation configuration uses forms outside it).
The content domain's population creators write from one real news corpus; originality therefore uses a 90% shingle threshold, and the reference composes from the same corpus.
Content difficulty 4 (10M viewers) is defined and its world spec built (internet population profile); no 10M-individual content run was made here.
Community and content worlds run the shared space's text path (Qwen3-0.6B LM): their long runs belong in GPU slots; the slot queue was congested during this wave, see test_results_unofficial.

Community: the population's community model (CORE-POP pop_social) joins and contributes far above usual participation inequality (an idle founder's generic community: 150 members and 108 weekly contributors after 9 days; a keyword-stuffed community: 501 members after 10 days); I-1 answers with an organiser-presence rule in the evaluator and member exit to successor communities (commlife), which halved the spam community in 10 days, but the population model itself needs calibration.
Content: keyword-stuffed posts still reach viewers (54 distinct viewers in 2 days against 217 for the reference); the level-1 target is 500 of 1,500 individuals.
integration_notes: CIV: add the domain population modules to crucible.civ.generator.ORDER after their owners so the domains compose into Tier 3 with population activity: scipop after sci (needs pop, docs), devpop after pkg (needs code, issues, pop), commlife after community (needs pop, social_ids). sci's `challenge` config (standards bureau) is off unless configured.

Workstream A / services: services/code.py create_repo derives the repository name with owner.split(':', 1)[1], which raises IndexError for population principals p<i> (no colon) and fails the whole population tick; devpop works around it with one account organisation per developer (o:dev<i>, founded through the identity module). The same applies to pkg.register's issue project owner handle.

CORE-POP: pop_social's community join model admits many members into a new community with a generic subject and no activity (probe: 'anything and everything' gathered 65-100 members and 20 contributors in 1-3 days, also beside 4 seeded communities); subject affinity of generic text may need a specificity term.
CORE-POP: population.core.money_deposit is used by scipop/devpop to fund individuals before they pay through tools (as economy.popbridge.fund does); a public export would avoid importing core.

domfw (I-fw): civ_recipe keeps civ params (log_retain 300,000); long domain runs exceeded it and base.run's count_events then failed (events before the in-memory window); I-1 domains set log_retain 3,000,000. A framework default for Tier 2 runs would help other domains.

domfw (I-fw): ScriptedReference is not used by I-1 references; they are generator scripts (domains/_t2kit.ScriptPolicy: act/observe/burst, tool results only) that base.reads_world scans like any policy class.

CIV: content's back-catalogue module `catalogue` (domains.content_domain) belongs after content/studio/aud/feed in crucible.civ.generator.ORDER when content worlds compose into Tier 3 (like scipop/devpop/commlife).

GOALS (crucible.goals.metrics): the I-1 domain files register their evaluator metrics at import (startup_sustainable_business, startup_qualifying_arr_usd, software_independent_adopters, content_original_viewers, community_sustained_participation, community_active_members, research_validated_discovery, research_discovery_accuracy) without a subject and add them to EVALUATOR_ONLY_METRICS; a public registration helper for evaluator-only metrics would be cleaner than mutating the set.

Owners of shared modules (dice, SP-9.16): base.dice_scan counts unregistered failure draws in worlds of I-1 domains: commerce/rivals.py:152 and services/cloud.py:681 (startup), social/popsocial.py:287 and :293 (content, community); none in the I-1 domain files.
